jlpt.title: JLPT simulation
jlpt.description: Free, timed JLPT mock exams for Kana, N5, N4 and N3 with the real structure, breaks between sections and a score report. Unofficial practice.
jlpt.lead: Same structure, timing and scoring scale as the real exam. The sections come in order, each with its own timer.
jlpt.rule.1: Skip and return to any question within a section using the question map.
jlpt.rule.2: Once a section is finalized you can't go back to it.
jlpt.rule.3: A 1-minute break follows each section (optional up to 15 minutes).
jlpt.rule.kana: Kana is a site-only level: pass with 60% overall and at least 40% in each section.

jlpt.tips.title: Before you start
jlpt.tips.1.title: Resist the restart
jlpt.tips.1.text: A bad first question is normal. Keep going: a full run tells you more than a perfect start.
jlpt.tips.2.title: Don't get stuck
jlpt.tips.2.text: If a question takes too long, pick your best guess, flag it with F and come back at the end.
jlpt.tips.3.title: Manage your energy
jlpt.tips.3.text: Use the breaks. Stand up, drink some water and look away from the screen.
jlpt.tips.4.title: Mistakes are valuable
jlpt.tips.4.text: Every wrong answer comes with an explanation at the end. That review is where you learn most.
jlpt.disclaimer: Unofficial practice simulation. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or a substitute for the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test administered by the Japan Foundation and JEES.

voice.help.open: How to add a Japanese voice
voice.help.title: Add a Japanese voice
voice.help.intro: Listening uses the Japanese voice of your device. Some browsers and systems don't include one. Open the section for your system, then close and reopen the browser.
voice.help.quick: Quickest fix: on a computer, open the site in Microsoft Edge (natural Japanese voices) or Google Chrome (“Google 日本語”). Brave, Opera and Firefox only use the voices installed on the system.
voice.help.windows.2: Under Manage voices, choose Add voices, pick Japanese (日本語) and install it.
voice.help.windows.3: Restart the browser and press Test audio again.
voice.help.mac.1: Open System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content.
voice.help.mac.2: Next to System voice, choose Manage Voices…, open Japanese and download Kyoko or Otoya.
voice.help.mac.3: Restart the browser and press Test audio again.
voice.help.android.1: Open Settings and search for “Text-to-speech output”.
voice.help.android.2: Choose Speech Services by Google, open its settings → Install voice data → Japanese.
voice.help.ios.1: Open Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices.
voice.help.ios.2: Choose Japanese and download a voice.
voice.help.ios.3: Close Safari completely and open the page again.
voice.help.linux.1: Browsers use speech-dispatcher, which rarely has a natural Japanese voice.
voice.help.linux.2: Chrome or Chromium with an internet connection usually offers “Google 日本語”.
voice.help.description: How to add a Japanese text-to-speech voice on Windows, macOS, Android, iPhone and Linux so Listen and the JLPT listening questions play.
